title: Gateway/control-plane attribution for KV cache telemetry v2 (route/model/version/region)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Problem
- KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 is only useful if we can reliably segment by tenant, route, model+version, region, and deployment mode.
- Today, cache events emitted from the runtime don’t consistently carry the gateway/control-plane context (route/model pin/version, edge region, deployment mode). This causes:
  - misleading hit-rate/hit-bytes by model (model routing fallbacks appear as misses)
  - inability to answer “which route regressed” without high-cardinality request_id tagging
  - Private deployments missing required fields due to reduced/absent control-plane integration

Goal
Attach a consistent attribution envelope to cache telemetry events at the gateway/control-plane boundary, aligned with the v2 spec + ADR cardinality budget. Ensure graceful behavior for Private (VPC/on-prem) where some fields may be absent.

Scope
1) Define the gateway-side attribution envelope for cache telemetry events (fields + fallbacks).
2) Populate fields from:
   - gateway request context (tenant, route, deployment mode)
   - routing decision (selected model_id/model_class; fallback reason)
   - runtime response headers (runtime_region; model_revision if available)
   - control-plane lookups (model revision metadata when available) with tight timeouts
3) Enforce cardinality controls per standards (no request_id label, hashed/bucketed route dimension where required).
4) Private compatibility: do not assume centralized control plane; support “unknown”/hashed IDs with explicit semantics.

Non-goals
- Changing cache algorithm behavior.
- Building a customer-facing UI.
- Adding new control-plane services; this should be enrichment using existing routing/control-plane APIs and runtime headers.

Proposed attribution envelope (gateway -> telemetry)
Required (always present; may be set to __unknown)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- region: edge region string for Hosted/Dedicated; for Private use "private" (not cluster id)
- tenant_key: hosted/dedicated uses tenant_id; private uses tenant_hash (stable salted hash)
- model_class: e.g., llama, mistral, qwen (low-cardinality)
- model_id: Redwood canonical model id/slug (bounded set; must not be raw OSS checkpoint path)
- model_revision: pinned version/revision id when available; else __unknown
- route_dim: route_bucket (stable hash bucket of route_id; e.g., 0-1023)

Optional (sampled/debug events only; behind sampling + pipelines)
- route_id (raw UUID) and route_name (only if explicitly allowlisted by tenant; default off)
- routing_fallback_reason (enum)
- runtime_region (if distinct from edge region)

Implementation notes
- Enrichment point: gateway telemetry exporter just before emitting kv_cache.* events.
- Control-plane lookups:
  - Must be best-effort with a strict budget (p99 < 2ms added in gateway path; hard timeout 5ms).
  - Cache results in-process with TTL (e.g., 60s) keyed by (model_id, requested_revision).
  - If lookup misses/times out, emit model_revision=__unknown and increment an internal counter.
- Runtime interop:
  - Prefer runtime-provided model revision header when present (more accurate for fallbacks).
  - Older runtimes may not send it; must not break.

Private compatibility constraints
- Some Private installs do not run the full hosted control plane; routing + model catalogs can be local.
- Fields we cannot safely rely on:
  - tenant_id (may not exist): use tenant_hash derived from configured org key (salted; no raw customer identifiers).
  - region: use constant "private" to avoid exploding cardinality across cluster names.
  - route_id: may not exist or may be customer-defined strings; do not emit raw route_id by default. Use route_bucket only.
- Feature flag defaults:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: default ON in canary regions once ENG-4815 schema is live.
  - Private: default OFF; require explicit enablement via private config + docs.

Acceptance criteria
- For Hosted and Dedicated:
  - >99.9% of kv_cache v2 events have deployment_mode, region, tenant_key, model_id, model_class, route_bucket populated (not empty).
  - model_revision populated for >=95% of events in canary (remaining are true unknowns/timeouts); missingness is measurable via metric.
  - No request_id tag introduced on metrics.
- For Private:
  - Events are emitted without control-plane dependency; missing fields resolve to __unknown/private-safe values.
  - No raw customer identifiers (tenant name, cluster name, route strings) are emitted by default.
- Cardinality:
  - No unbounded labels added; route_id/route_name remain debug-only with sampling/allowlist.
- Docs/operability:
  - Add a short note to the rollout playbook on Private defaults and expected “unknown” behavior.

Testing plan
- Unit tests:
  - attribute envelope creation given various request contexts
  - fallbacks when control-plane lookup times out
  - private mode sanitization (no raw identifiers)
- Integration tests:
  - older runtime (no model_revision header) still produces valid events
  - routing fallback path: model_id differs from requested; we still tag selected model
- Data validation:
  - compare gateway-side model_revision distribution vs routing logs in canary

Links
- Confluence: kv-cache-telemetry-v2 metric spec (v2 tagging + required fields)
- ADR: ADR-027 KV cache metric cardinality budget
- Linear: ENG-4815 (pipeline/schema + guardrails), ENG-4813/4814 (runtime event hooks + outcome classification)

Open questions
- Do we need a dedicated low-cardinality "route_type" (api route vs console eval vs internal) in addition to route_bucket? (Logan requesting)
- For Dedicated: should region be the customer’s chosen region or the physical runtime region if they run multi-region active/active? (Ethan/Mina to confirm)

Owner(s)
- Assignee: Amara Diallo (gateway)
- Reviewers: Ethan Park (control plane), Mina Haddad (routing), Nadia Rahman (pipeline/cardinality)
comments: 2025-02-07 (Logan Wright): Creating this as the glue between runtime cache events and dashboards. Without route/model/version/region attribution the hit-rate dashboard is basically unusable. Please align with ADR-027 on route dimension (bucketed by default).

2025-02-10 (Amara Diallo): Drafted a GatewayTelemetryEnricher interface that takes (req_ctx, routing_decision, runtime_headers) -> attrs. Biggest gap is model_revision: routing has requested revision but fallbacks happen post-routing. Plan is to prefer runtime header (selected_revision) when present and fall back to routing decision otherwise.

2025-02-11 (Ethan Park): For Hosted/Dedicated, control-plane can supply canonical revision ids, but do NOT do synchronous lookups per request. Cache + strict timeout only. For Private, please avoid any assumptions about tenant_id; use configured stable hash.

2025-02-13 (Mina Haddad): Route dimension: we should not ship raw route_name on metrics. If Optimize needs top routes, do it in the pipeline with top-K per tenant and aggregate the rest. Gateway can include route_id only on sampled debug events (traces/logs).

2025-02-17 (Amara Diallo): Implemented: deployment_mode/region/tenant_key/model_id/model_class/route_bucket. model_revision is wired from runtime header if present; otherwise __unknown. Added counters: cache_telemetry_attr_missing_total{field=...} and cache_telemetry_cp_lookup_timeout_total.

2025-02-18 (Nadia Rahman): Please keep label names exactly per spec. Also confirm tenant_key format: hosted/dedicated should be numeric id, private should be a fixed-length hex. Pipeline will treat them differently for joins; don’t mix.

2025-02-20 (Amara Diallo): Added private sanitization: region="private" constant; tenant_key uses SHA256(salt||org_key) truncated to 16 bytes hex; route_bucket = murmur3(route_key)%1024. Feature flags: gateway.cache_telemetry_v2_attr.enabled and gateway.cache_telemetry_v2_attr.debug_route_id_sample_rate.

2025-02-22 (Amara Diallo): In review internally. Next: add integration test fixture for older runtime headers + update rollout notes for Private defaults. Blocking on final label spellings from Logan/Thomas (ADR enforcement).
